audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Level 1, Levels 4-5 and Level 6 to 'Skill' and then handed Renekton the 2+ item stage — the exact inverse of the page's own prose, which says 'Level 1 you are the aggressor' and 'By 2+ items... stop taking extended solo duels'. The packet chart reads Renekton 1 through 6, Swain at 2+ items.
audit.why: Swain has no dash and a telegraphed root; Renekton owns every lane stage. Past two items the drain plus soul stacks outlast his burst, so that row belongs to Swain.
audit.corrected: Levels 1, 4-5 and 6 flipped to Renekton, and 2+ items flipped to Swain (3/10), in both layers as one atomic group.

audit.why: Levels 2-3, level 6 Dominus, first item, and Swain's 2-item Rylai's/Liandry's drain — four spikes matching where power actually moves.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two omissions. (1) Nevermove is described only as an 'E pull' with a cast animation. Riot's text: it launches forward, then RETURNS to Swain and roots enemies it hits on the way back — the return pass is what you dodge, and the page never says so. (2) Demonic Ascension is described as something you can wait out; Riot's text says the form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions, so it does not simply expire while he is on top of you.
audit.why: Both change the decision. Sidestepping the outgoing wave and standing still is how players eat the root, and 'bait it and let it expire' fails if he keeps draining you.
audit.corrected: Return-pass root written into breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[1].d, report[5].t and wants.you[1]; the indefinite-drain condition written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and mid.

edits.before: Fury autos bully the first waves. Identify how Swain contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Fury autos bully the first waves — Death's Hand is all he has and Nevermove is not up, so step up and harass.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Demonic Ascension's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: The lane-control window: he has no dash, so trade whenever Nevermove is spent — 12s at rank 1 — and bank the health lead you build.

edits.before: Dominus stats turn even fights into wins before 25 minutes. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Swain's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Dominus HP absorbs the drain long enough to stun and burst — but if Demonic Ascension is already active, do not dash in at all.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Swain carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in and the drain outlasts your burst — carry threat 8/10, so lock him down for your team instead of dueling him.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Burst him before it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Swain Demonic Ascension: 120s, and it lasts as long as he keeps draining champions — it does not simply time out. - Nevermove: 12s at rank 1, and the root lands on the RETURN pass. - Dominus: 120s, kill windows only.

edits.before: His drain. Burst him before it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: The drain persists while he holds champions in it — burst before he casts.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the return pass — watch the wave come back.

edits.before: Track Swain's Demonic Ascension: His drain. Burst him before it. When it is down — W-stun + Q him.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the return pass, not the outgoing one — 12s at rank 1. Burst him before R.

edits.before: Side-step or walk around his E pull cast animation so he loses his only root and cannot safely activate R
edits.after: Dodge Nevermove on its return pass, not the outgoing one — that is where the root lands and his R setup dies

edits.before: From levels 4-6 the lane is yours to close out. His Demonic Ascension at level 6 is the moment to respect — the drain is substantial and he activates it the instant you engage, so your all-in must be committed and fast: slice in, empowered W immediately to interrupt his animation and front-load the stun, Q through him for the heal, and only extend the fight while he is stunned. Your own R gives you the HP buffer to absorb the drain for the stun window and still come out ahead. If he pops R before you engage, do not E in — the active drain plus soul-stack healing means he wins a protracted fight; bait the R activation by faking an engage, let it expire, then run the real all-in.
edits.after: From levels 4-6 the lane is yours to close out. Demonic Ascension at 6 is the moment to respect — it is 120s, he activates it the instant you engage, and the form persists as long as he is draining a champion, so it will not time out while you stand in it. Your all-in must be fast: slice in, empowered W to front-load the 1.5s stun, Q through him for the heal, and extend only while he is stunned. Dominus buffers the drain for that window. If he pops R first, do not E in — walk out of the 650 radius instead, break the drain, and run the real all-in once he is alone.

notes: The chart was inverted against its own prose on four rows and is now aligned with both the packet and the text. Two mechanics were missing: Nevermove roots on the return pass (the reason 'sidestep the cast' advice gets players rooted anyway) and Demonic Ascension does not expire while he keeps draining a champion — so the old 'bait it and let it expire' line was wrong and is replaced with breaking the 650 drain radius.
